 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the appellants/petitioners challenging the common judgment and award dated 30.10.2017 passed by the Court of the IV Addl. Dist. Judge and Member MACT No.XIII at Vijayapur (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.1783/2015, on the ground of inadequate and meager compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are; the petitioners are wife, children and mother of the deceased Arunoday @ Arun Gudadinni.

That on 04.11.2015 at about 3.30 a.m. when the husband of first appellant-Arunoday @ Arun and others were travelling in Mahindra Bolero Jeep bearing No.KA-28-N-7825 from Vijayapura to Almatti, driver of the said Jeep drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and came near Kudagi Power Grid, lost his control and dashed against road divider which resulted in accident.
In the said accident, the husband of first claimant-appellant herein sustained grievous injuries and died on spot due to accidental injuries.
4. It is stated that the deceased-Arunodaya was hale and healthy and was aged about 50 years.
He was doing mason work and thereby getting monthly income of `25,000/-.
The deceased was the only earning member of the family who used to look after the petitioners and, the family was depending on his income.
In view of the sudden and untimely death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their sole bread earner, love and affection and also have suffered mentally and financially.
Hence, they filed a claim petition seeking compensation.

5. On service of notice, respondent-Insurance Company appeared and detailed statement of objections to the claim petition denying inter alia age, avocation and income including the death of deceased as alleged in the claim petition.

It is further stated in the objection that, respondent no.2 issued private car package policy to respondent no.1, respondent no.2-Insurance company has not collected extra premium from respondent no.1. to cover the risk of the passengers travelling in the vehicle.
Further it is pleaded that the accident was not due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of insured vehicle.
Hence, on this basis, sought for dismissal of claim petition.
6. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the wife of the deceased examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P6.
Respondent-Insurance Company examined its official as RW.1 and Ex.R-1 Insurance policy is marked.

7. On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary, the Tribunal fastened liability on the respondent-Insurance Company and awarded total compensation of `9,55,000/- with 6%
interest per annum and directed the respondent-Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount within 30 days from the date of award.

8. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for the claimants/petitioners that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is erroneous, contrary to the material evidence placed on record and the documents presented by the petitioners.
9. Learned counsel further contends that the Tribunal has gone wrong in making assessment of income to the extent of `7,500/- per month whereas, the income ought to have been taken at `25,000/-.
Even if that is not taken, the Tribunal ought to have assessed the income according to the notional income chart value of `13,750/- for the accident of the year 2020.

Learned counsel further contends that the Tribunal has awarded meager compensation under other heads and has not awarded just and reasonable compensation which also requires interference at the hands of this Court.

entities.text: Smt. Geeta And Ors vs Mallikarjun @ Malakajappa And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel further contends that the Tribunal has not awarded suitable compensation under the head 'loss of consortium' to all the dependants/legal representatives of the deceased.
He further contends that the Tribunal has committed a gross error in not adding 'loss of future prospects' to the income to the deceased.
On these grounds, they seek enhancement of compensation and consequently allow the appeal.

11. Per contra, learned counsel Sri Manvendra Reddy, appearing on behalf of respondent-Insurance Company vehemently contends that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is in consonance with the material evidence placed on record and the same in fact is on the higher side.

Learned counsel further contends that the award of compensation on the other heads are suitably calculated and rightly awarded, which does not call for interference and on the basis of these submissions, he seeks to dismiss the appeal filed by the petitioners.
12.

Having heard the learned counsel for the appellants/petitioners and learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company, the points that would arise for consideration before this Court are:
i) Whether the claimants are entitled to enhancement of compensation ?
ii) What order"
13.

On a careful perusal of entire material on record and having gone through the impugned judgment and award including the exhibits marked in the case on hand, it is apparently seen that the petitioners would be entitled for enhancement of compensation for the reason stated herein below:-
(a) It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 04.11.2015 at 3.30 a.m. because of accident occurred due to speedy driving of Bolero vehicle by its driver.
These aspects have been proved by way of production of Ex.P1 to P6.
Admittedly, there is no challenge made to the initiation of criminal prosecution and laying of charge-sheet.
The Insurance Company has not filed any appeal against the judgment and award.

Under the circumstances, there is no requirement for this Court to delve into the occurrence of accident, involvement of the vehicles and so also the death of deceased Arunoday Gudadinni having occurred due to the road traffic accident.
(b) Now, the question that is to be decided by this Court is whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is meager and whether calls for interference by this Court.

It is relevant to quote the decision in Syed Basheer Ahmed vs. Mohammed Zameer1 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court noticed that Sec.168 of the MV Act enjoins the claims Tribunal to make an award determining "the amount of compensation which appears to be just".

sentences.text: However, the objective factors, which may constitute the basis of compensation appearing as just, have not been indicated in the Act.

Thus, the expression "which appears to be just"

4 vests wide discretion in the Claims Tribunal in the matter of determination of compensation.

sentences.text: Nevertheless, the wide amplitude of such power does not empower the Tribunal to determine the compensation arbitrarily or to ignore settled principles relating to the determination of the compensation.

Similarly, although the Act is a beneficial legislation, it can (2009) 2 SCC 225 neither be allowed to be used as a source of profit nor as a windfall to the persons affected nor should it be punitive to the persons liable to pay compensation.

The determination of the compensation must be based on certain data, establishing reasonable nexus between the loss incurred by the dependents of the deceased and the compensation to be awarded to them.
In a nutshell, the amount of compensation determined to be payable to the petitioners has to be fair and reasonable by accepted legal standards.

(c) The determination of the quantum must answer what "contemporary society would deem to be a fair sum such as would allow the wrong doer to hold up his head among his neighbours and say with their approval that he has done the fair thing".
The amount awarded must not be niggardly since the "law values life and limb in a free Society in generous case".
At the same time, misplaced sympathy, generosity and benevolence cannot be the guiding factor for determining compensation.

The object of providing compensation is to please the petitioners to the extent possible, in almost the same financial position as they were in before the accident and not to make a fortune out of misfortune that has befallen them.
(d) On the basis of the material evidence placed before this Court, it is seen that the deceased was aged about 50 years and doing business and agriculture work and earning `25,000/- per month.
We are in agreement with the learned counsel for the appellants that, `8,000/- requires to be taken as monthly income and same is taken.
The deceased being aged 50 years is entitled to 25% towards future prospects in addition to the notional income chart value for assessment of income.

In view of the fact that the deceased was aged 50 years, the appropriate multiplier would be '13'
which is rightly taken by the Tribunal.
Same does not call for interference.

(e) Addition of 25% towards loss of future prospects to be added as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and others2, which would be `10,000/-
(`8,000/- + 2,000 (25% of 8,000)).

and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another3, which would be `7,500 (`10,000/- (-)
2,500 (1/4rd)) and the appropriate multiplier is '13'.

(f) We are in agreement with the contentions of the learned counsel for petitioners that the Tribunal has not awarded appropriate amount towards consortium.

Since there are four dependants being the wife, son, daughter and mother of deceased, they each be entitled to `40,000/- per head as Smt. Geeta And Ors vs Mallikarjun @ Malakajappa And Anr on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166199778/

(g) Towards 'loss of estate' and towards 'transportation of dead body & funeral expenses', petitioners would be entitled to `15,000/- each i.e., a sum of `30,000/- requires to be awarded and it is accordingly awarded.
Accordingly, under conventional head `1,90,000/- (loss of consortium `1,60,000/- + loss of estate `15,000/- + Towards transportation of dead body & funeral expenses `15,000/-) is awarded.
(h) As per the decision in Pranay Sethi, stated supra, 10% on the conventional head for each block period requires to be awarded, which in the present case would be `19,000/- for one block period.

In all, the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation in a sum of `13,79,000/- as against a sum of `9,55,000/-, as detailed in the table below:

14.
So far as liability is concerned, it is proved that, because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Mahindra Bolero Vehicle, the accident has occurred.
The vehicle in question was insured with respondent-Insurance Company.

Further, the Tribunal has recorded a finding that in the evidence of RW.1 an official of the Insurance Company never disputed that driver of the offending Jeep was not having valid and effective DL on the date and time of accident.

Thus, it is clear that respondent no.1 is the owner of the Jeep in question and the same is insured with respondent no.2-Insurance Company as on the date and time of the accident as per Ex.R.1 the Insurance Policy.
Thus, the Tribunal has held respondent no.1 primarily liable to pay the compensation to the claimants.
However, respondent no.2 Insurance Company shall indemnify respondent no.1 in payment of compensation.

Resultantly, we pass the following:
ORDER

The Judgment and Award dated 30.10.2017 passed by the Member, M.A.C.T.XIII,
Vijayapura in so far as MVC claimants in No.1783/2015 is concerned, is modified.

The appellants-petitioners are held entitled for enhanced compensation of `4,24,000/- together with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization excluding the interest for the period of delay of 770 days in filing the appeal.
The respondent-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the said enhanced compensation before the M.A.C.T, Vijayapura within four weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.

On such deposit, the Tribunal to take appropriate steps to deposit the amount in the name of daughter and son of the deceased keeping their interest and also make payment as per the terms of apportionment so passed while passing the award.
Petitioner No.1 is entitled to draw periodical interest on such deposit.
